newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Sept 19.

text.p: Japan's four top life insurance companies -- Nippon Life Insurance Co, Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co, Sumitomo Life Insurance Co and Meiji Mutual Life Insurance Co -- plan to sell auto and fire insurance to large corporations through non-life insurance subsidiaries starting in October. These life insurers had previously planned to restrict their non-life subsidiaries from selling auto and fire insurance to large corporate customers for two or three years.

Leading cement producers have started to streamline their ready-mixed concrete subsidiaries. Japan's largest cement producer Chichibu Onoda Cement Corp is to cut the number of its plants to half the current number by March 31, 1998. Nihon Cement Co Ltd plans to streamline two or three plants into one company.

Akia Corp, a Tokyo-based personal computer venture, plans to start selling Macintosh-compatible notebook-type computers by the end of this year, with help from International Business Machines Corp. Akia will sub-license the Macintosh operating system (OS) from IBM, which has licensed the Macintosh system from Apple Computer Inc. Under the agreement, IBM will supply Akia with micro-processing units (MPU) for the PCs, while IBM Japan Ltd will help sales and provide services.
Electricity and gas companies plan to raise utility prices from next January for a third consecutive quarter

Nissho Iwai Corp plans to provide about 15.4 billion yen worth of loans to build a chemical plant in Indonesia. The plant would have a target annual output of 100,000 tonnes of octanol, which is used in the production of polyvinyl chloride materials.

Chugai Pharmaceutical Co Ltd plans to set up a joint venture to develop, manufacture and sell non-prescription medicine in Japan, in cooperation with Merck and Co Inc . The company will be established in Tokyo in October with initial capital of 10 million yen, to be increased to 2.5 billion yen when it starts operations next spring.
